title: How to Evaluate When You Don't Know How to Evaluate? Choosing Reliable Setups for Base Language Model Benchmarking
abstract: arXiv:2610.19185v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Evaluation of large language models (LLMs) remains largely pre-scientific: it involves many design decisions, with little guidance on how to make them. These choices can substantially affect measured performance and, consequently, decisions about subsequent pretraining. To identify effective evaluation setups, we investigate 8 aspects, such as task formulation or the number of in-context examples. We compare the setups using three widely-used signal criteria, repurposed as normative meta-measures: monotonicity, non-randomness, and ranking consistency of the evaluation scores across intermediate checkpoints. In an early pretraining scenario, we evaluate these setups on 26 monolingual 2B-parameter models trained on different types of data, using 80 tasks in four languages. translated_title: 当你不知道如何评估时该如何评估？为基础语言模型基准测试选择可靠的评估设置
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）的评估在很大程度上仍处于前科学阶段：它涉及许多设计决策，而关于如何做出这些决策却缺乏指导。这些选择可能会显著影响测得的性能，进而影响关于后续预训练的决策。为了确定有效的评估设置，我们研究了8个方面，例如任务表述方式或上下文示例的数量。我们使用三种广泛使用的信号标准来比较这些设置，并将其重新用作规范性的元度量：评估分数在中间检查点之间的单调性、非随机性和排名一致性。在早期预训练场景中，我们在26个在不同类型数据上训练的单语2B参数模型上评估了这些设置，使用了四种语言的80个任务。我们还在相同四种语言的三个更大的LLM（≥7B）上检验了这些设置，并探讨了首选设置如何随模型规模变化。我们的结果得出（结论）……
tldr: 本研究系统考察了任务表述、上下文示例数量等8个评估设计维度，并利用单调性、非随机性和排名一致性三种元度量标准，为基础语言模型在早期预训练阶段选择可靠的基准测试设置提供指导。
en_tdlr: This study systematically investigates 8 evaluation design aspects, such as task formulation and the number of in-context examples, and uses three meta-measures—monotonicity, non-randomness, and ranking consistency—to identify reliable benchmarking setups for base language models in early pretraining scenarios.
